## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Title: Fix inverted and off-by-one grant check in `isAccessTokenId` matcher

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-492

Explanation:
The encoded prefix is laid out as `[0..2)` session type, `[2..4)` token type, and `[4..6)` grant type. The matcher has two bugs:

- **Wrong slice.** It takes `substring(3, 5)`. For example, `"onrtac"` yields `"ta"`, which is never a valid grant shortcut.
- **Inverted condition.** It returns `false` when the slice *equals* the expected shortcut.

Because the wrong slice never matches, the inverted check never fires. The matcher therefore accepts any grant shortcut, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken` and the device variant verify nothing about the grant type. If the slice is ever corrected without also fixing the condition, every valid token would fail.

It also does not check that the prefix has length 6. A shorter prefix would throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of producing a clean mismatch.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
String[] items = item.split(":");
if (items.length != 2 || items[0].length() != 6) return false;
if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
return isUUID().matches(items[1]);
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Null check validates `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:70-73

Explanation:
Line 73 calls `requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. A null `rawTokenId` is therefore accepted, and later encoding produces IDs like `onrtac:null`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Shortcut length is not enforced; 3-letter shortcuts (as documented) break decoding

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:65-86
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81,109-117

Explanation:
The Javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". The decoder, however, requires an encoded context of exactly 6 characters, meaning a 2-character grant shortcut.

A custom grant that follows the documentation would produce tokens that encode successfully. Any later call to `getTokenContextFromTokenId` on those tokens would throw `IllegalArgumentException`.

Nothing validates shortcut length:
- not in `postInit`,
- not during the lazy refresh in `getShortcutByGrantType`,
- not in `encodeTokenId`.

The lazy refresh also skips the uniqueness check, so a late-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites an existing mapping.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// Javadoc: "Must be exactly 2 characters and unique across grants."
// In postInit and lazy refresh:
if (grantShortcut == null || grantShortcut.length() != 2) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Grant " + grantName + " must have a 2-char shortcut");
}
if (grantsByShortcuts.containsKey(grantShortcut) && !grantName.equals(grantsByShortcuts.get(grantShortcut))) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Duplicate grant shortcut " + grantShortcut);
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Maintainability
Title: Breaking SPI change: new abstract `getShortcut()` and removed `Context(Context)` constructor

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:99-103

Explanation:
`getShortcut()` is added as an abstract interface method. Every third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` will fail to compile, or will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime in `postInit`.

The public copy constructor `Context(Context)` is also removed without deprecation. Any extension or internal caller that relies on it will break. I can't see those callers in this diff, so please verify.

A safer approach is to provide a default implementation of `getShortcut()`. Alternatively, handle a missing shortcut by falling back to `UNKNOWN` instead of throwing `IllegalStateException` in `encodeTokenId`. Throwing there turns every token issuance for that grant into a 500.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
default String getShortcut() {
    return null; // encoder falls back to "na"
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Every access token issuance now depends on `session.getContext().getClient()` and may use the wrong client

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54-55
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1052-1054
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84-87

Explanation:
`getShouldUseLightweightToken` was previously called only from protocol mappers. It is now called from `initToken` for every access token.

It reads the lightweight flag from `session.getContext().getClient()` rather than from the client the token is issued for. This causes two problems:

- **NPE risk.** Any code path that builds tokens without a context client now fails with a `NullPointerException`. Examples include internal or admin-generated tokens, and flows that set the client after token creation.
- **Wrong token type.** In flows where the context client differs from the token's client, such as token exchange, the encoded token type can be wrong.

Use `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient()` for the client attribute, and null-guard the context.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
ClientModel client = clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient();
Object attr = session.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED);
boolean useLightweightToken = Boolean.parseBoolean(client.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED))
        || Boolean.TRUE.equals(attr);
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: `grantType` is captured once in the constructor and goes stale after `setFormParams`; NPE on null `formParams`

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102-105

Explanation:
`grantType` is read from `formParams` in the constructor. `setFormParams` replaces the form params but does not update `grantType`.

The constructor also dereferences `formParams` without a null check, which previously was not required. Either derive `grantType` lazily in `getGrantType()`, or refresh it inside `setFormParams` and null-guard the constructor.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
public String getGrantType() {
    return formParams == null ? null : formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);
}
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Unknown shortcuts in attacker-supplied token IDs trigger a full factory scan on every lookup

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:121-137

Explanation:
`getGrantTypeByShortcut` streams all grant factories on every cache miss. Token IDs come from client-supplied tokens, so repeatedly presenting bogus shortcuts forces a scan per request.

The cost is minor, but negative results should be cached. Alternatively, rely on the provider factory's deployment-change hooks instead of lazily scanning on each miss.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// Cache misses, or rebuild the maps only on ProviderEvent (deployment change) instead of per-miss scans.
~~~
